topic.subject: chemistry
topic.title: Properties of metals and reactions with acids, oxygen and water
topic.overview: Metals share useful physical properties but differ greatly in reactivity. Recognising reaction patterns and observations allows products and relative reactivity to be predicted.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Typical metals conduct heat and electricity, are strong, shiny when freshly cut, malleable and usually have high melting points.
Typical non-metals are poorer conductors and, when solid, are often brittle; there are exceptions.
reactive metal + water -> metal hydroxide + hydrogen in the simple Year 8 pattern
Faster fizzing, greater temperature rise or faster gas production indicates a faster reaction only when conditions are controlled.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: an element with characteristic properties such as electrical conductivity and malleability
an element lacking the typical set of metallic properties
able to be hammered or pressed into shape
able to be drawn into wires
a material through which heat or electric charge transfers readily
a compound of a metal and oxygen
the gaseous product of many metal-acid reactions
how readily a substance undergoes a chemical reaction

practicals.title: Compare metal reactivity with acid
practicals.aim: Compare how rapidly equal metal samples react with dilute acid.
practicals.variables: IV: metal identity; DV: gas volume in fixed time or time for a fixed volume; controls: mass/surface area, acid volume/concentration, temperature.
practicals.method: Add equal prepared metal samples to equal acid volumes, collect gas with a gas syringe, record at fixed intervals and repeat.
practicals.expectedResult: More reactive metals produce hydrogen faster under identical conditions; some may show little or no reaction.
practicals.safety: Wear eye protection, keep away from flames because hydrogen is flammable and use small dilute quantities.
practicals.evaluation: Use a gas syringe rather than judging bubbles, standardise surface area, repeat and calculate means.

commonMistakes: Assuming every metal reacts vigorously with cold water.
Naming hydrogen as the product of metal plus oxygen.
Comparing different-sized metal pieces and calling the result fair.
examTips: Use the reaction pattern before naming the salt.
When comparing rate, demand equal quantity and surface area.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.topic: Properties of metals and reactions with acids, oxygen and water
practicals.title: Compare metal reactivity with acid
practicals.aim: Compare how rapidly equal metal samples react with dilute acid.
practicals.variables: IV: metal identity; DV: gas volume in fixed time or time for a fixed volume; controls: mass/surface area, acid volume/concentration, temperature.
practicals.method: Add equal prepared metal samples to equal acid volumes, collect gas with a gas syringe, record at fixed intervals and repeat.
practicals.expectedResult: More reactive metals produce hydrogen faster under identical conditions; some may show little or no reaction.
practicals.safety: Wear eye protection, keep away from flames because hydrogen is flammable and use small dilute quantities.
practicals.evaluation: Use a gas syringe rather than judging bubbles, standardise surface area, repeat and calculate means.
